label: Reconstructed 1835 workwear studies referenced to existing resident records
source_scope: Newspaper terminology only for chicago_american_1835: transcription-mediated nearby June/July 1835 advertisements mention shirts, vests, pantaloons and round jackets; the July 4 advertisement postdates July 1 and does not attest an exact outfit or before-scene stock. The two directly read Mount 1835 reproduction sources are qualitative period analogies for fuller hanging lower trousers and closed lower waistcoat fronts. Their year-only painting dates do not establish completion before 1835-07-01, exact Chicago outfits or named likenesses. No page/image pixels, painted garment tracing or measured patterns enter the model.
basis: Original garment shells fitted to the cleared anonymous adult base. Shirt, separate waistcoat, high-waisted trousers and closed shoes are a bounded reconstruction. Pattern/cut, seams, layer ease, colors, buttons, wear and body shape are unmeasured choices; not an attested uniform or photographic character.
material_limitations: Generic cleared CC0 body skin atlas remains; original procedural opaque brown iris atlas now supplies reconstructed sclera/iris/pupil components. Cloth and shoes still use original coarse PBR colors/procedural linen micro-pattern without measured period fabric, captured leather, seams or photographic material qualification. Skin/eyes/hair/clothing are provisional reconstructions, not a named photographic likeness.
validation_status: T1789 modular wardrobe source candidate: three explicit existing-resident assemblies with connected waistcoats, physical edge returns, fitted buttons, optional short work jackets/lapels and fitted hats. Fresh canonical output, continuous fit, LOD, period/material and actual photo-quality review remain required; no old source proof qualifies this change.
